tasks.instruction: The update was accepted, but callers still receive the old version. Release version 2 on the existing worker without reducing the application’s declared CPU request.

hints.title: Account for overlap during updates
hints.body: A rolling update can create a new pod before removing the old one. maxSurge controls extra pods; maxUnavailable controls how many desired replicas may be unavailable. Does the single worker have room for both CPU requests?

hints.title: Trade a short outage for progress
hints.body: Keep the 1000m CPU request and one desired replica. Set maxSurge to 0 and maxUnavailable to 1 in candidate.yaml so Terraform can apply a release that removes the old pod before starting the new one. This lab accepts a brief outage; explain why a production service might need extra capacity instead.

tasks.title: Explain the prevention measure

questions.prompt: There is only enough worker capacity for one app pod. What tradeoff lets a new version replace the old one without adding a worker?
options: Temporarily stop the old pod before starting the new one, accepting a short interruption
Keep both pods running without changing capacity
Treat the healthy old response as a successful new release
questions.explanation: An update that allows no extra pod but allows one unavailable pod can progress within this budget. With a single desired replica, that means a short outage. Production availability requirements may justify spare capacity instead.

13-public-access.objective: Trace a real HTTP request from your laptop to the app, repair the blocked public path through Terraform, and prove that path is closed after cleanup.

stages.title: Define success
stages.summary: Reuse the Game 07 worker and its public IPv4. Add one rule allowing only your laptop’s current public IPv4 (/32 means exactly one IPv4 address). No load balancer, new VM or NAT gateway. This is a static HTTP exercise, not a production website.

tasks.title: State the delivery contract
tasks.instruction: Trace a real HTTP request from your laptop to the app, repair the blocked public path through Terraform, and prove that path is closed after cleanup.
tasks.success: One existing worker, a NodePort Service, and one Terraform-owned ingress rule restricted to the laptop’s /32. Prove the public HTTP path opens, then closes during cleanup.

tasks.title: Prepare a short, scoped session
tasks.instruction: Use arcade start 13 and run the read-only preflight from the laptop that will send curl. It checks account, cluster, worker and security-group ownership before writing the exact inputs. Keep the $20 total budget and remove the rule at the end.
tasks.success: The recorded account, cluster, worker and laptop address match the intended test. You know which state owns the rule and which owns the workload.

tasks.success: Both saved plans have the expected scope. Internal HTTP returns arcade-public-ok; starter mode’s external curl fails before the repair.

tasks.title: Record the first observation
tasks.instruction: Record both a successful internal request and the failed external request. A failed login, wrong cluster, or unscheduled pod is a setup failure, not the intended public-path fault.
tasks.success: Save the internal response and external connection result from the same test session. A healthy internal app narrows the failed public path.

commands.code:
(
  set -euo pipefail
